A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoFO research and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Reformatting and renumbering do not prevent reliable content matching.

before.justification: V3 reports original instruction and continual fine-tuning experiments, optimizer comparisons, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: V4 retains those original results and adds coding, instruction-following, optimizer-comparison, and synthetic experimental results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same momentum filtering and Adam updates. The LoRA and Lion combinations and alternative parameter partitioning already appeared in v3. Replacing alpha-percent notation with alpha does not change the procedure.

E1.justification: V4 adds dedicated coding fine-tuning on Magicoder-Evol-Instruct and instruction-following fine-tuning on the filtered IFEval-like dataset, plus BBH evaluation. These extend the represented training data and task requirements beyond the retained math, medical, continual-learning, and general-capability evaluations.

E2.justification: V4 adds NAdam and RMSProp to the distance–forgetting comparison in Figure 10, and Adapter and BitFit to the MetaMathQA comparison in Table 11. Existing comparisons with LoRA, HFT, HMA, CoFiTune, soft-masking, and continual-learning methods remain.

E3.justification: Added protocols include training budgets of 0.1, 0.2, and more than three epochs; a ten-dimensional synthetic experiment with a learning-rate search and explicit convergence criterion; and loss/gradient evaluation on 512 examples from existing checkpoints. New coding, instruction-following, and PEFT comparisons also specify experimental settings. The retained main-table protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: V4 adds analyses of the distance–forgetting relationship across training stages and optimizers, a synthetic test of Example 1, and filtering-strategy ablations on instruction-following data. Appendix F.5 additionally examines whether regularization impedes optimization of the original loss, explicitly reusing Figure 5 checkpoints.

E5.justification: Appendix B.5 newly reports repeating the synthetic experiment across three random seeds. V3 contains no corresponding repeated-seed reporting. This addition is limited: Table 4 supplies no variability estimates, and the LLM results do not gain uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The earlier tables retain their numerical results, but v4 adds substantial new results in Tables 4, 8, 11, and 14 and Figures 8–10 and 15. For example, new coding results show HumanEval scores of 53.3 for MoFO versus 56.2 for Default FT, with general-capability averages of 51.4 versus 50.0. These are additional comparisons, not improvements over v3 under identical settings.

T1.justification: V4 adds an explicit norm-equivalence lemma and proof, then reformulates Theorem 1 using the existing top-alpha norm with consequences for all Lp norms. The assumptions, convergence order, filter-stability lemma, and Theorem 2 remain. The revised derivation also introduces an incorrect intermediate equality after Equation 15 in Appendix A.2.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: momentum filtering mitigates forgetting without pre-training data, preserves competitive fine-tuning performance, and admits convergence analysis. The added evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V4 qualifies the distance–forgetting relationship as clearer after roughly one epoch and discusses unstable early behavior, benchmark overlap, and stochasticity. It also adds substantive discussion of nonsmooth-objective limitations, possible explanations for regularization's weaker optimization, and the applicability of Adapter and BitFit to difficult LLM tasks.

D1.justification: V4 newly provides a MoFO code-repository link and documents data selection, access information, and hyperparameters for the added experiments, including the filtered IFEval-like subset and Adapter size search. The previously documented hardware, common training settings, and partition implementation remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 adds references supporting the new datasets, benchmarks, and comparators, and expands discussion of noise-stability regularization and nonsmooth optimization. Its established positioning as greedy block coordinate descent adapted to Adam remains. Moving Related Works into the main text is primarily structural.

P1.justification: The convergence discussion is extensively rewritten into a structured proof sketch, with an appendix roadmap and notation recap. Related Works moves from Appendix A to main Section 5, while the introduction, appendix organization, and cross-references are revised. These substantially change the explanatory structure beyond adding experiments.

P2.justification: V4 replaces the two-column main-text format with a single-column journal layout and substantially resizes and repositions displays. It adds four numbered figures and four tables, expands landscape captions to explain axes and color scales, and revises table emphasis. Existing displays are retained across renumbering.

improvement.justification: V4 broadens empirical validation, qualifies when proximity predicts retained capability, and improves access information and theoretical exposition. These provide an evidence-supported net benefit over v3. The gains are tempered by a new incorrect equality in Appendix A.2 and coding-result prose that claims superiority despite Table 8 showing lower HumanEval performance than Default FT. The core method, earlier results, and convergence framework remain intact.
